title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
source_system: Corporate secretary's entity management system
what_it_shows: A bank holding company supervised by the Federal Reserve and an SEC registrant, with three divisions. Cris Santos Bank, N.A. is a national bank supervised by the OCC with FDIC-insured deposits. Cris Santos Financial Technology, LLC is a nonbank subsidiary of the holding company, not of the bank. CRE Lending and Servicing (acquired in 2024) and Group Property Management are nonbank subsidiaries. Corporate shared services staff are employed by the holding company. The register lists no broker-dealer, investment adviser, investment company, transfer agent, insurance licensee, credit union, telecommunications carrier, or entity licensed in New York. Organization charts show the Group CISO reporting to the Group CIO, the Head of Technology and Cyber Risk to the Group Chief Risk Officer, the Chief Audit Executive to both audit committees, and a separate CISO in the Financial Software division

title: Group: HR roster by division
source_system: Group HR system
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees: Banking about 31,000, Financial Software about 5,500 (including 460 client support staff), Commercial Real Estate about 3,000 (including about 140 closing and funding staff), corporate shared services about 5,500. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger; FY2025 Form 10-K segment note
what_it_shows: Revenue of about $18.0 billion: Banking about $15.2 billion, Financial Software about $1.6 billion, Commercial Real Estate about $1.2 billion. The finance calendar counts about 250 business days a year

title: Group: regulatory reports of total consolidated assets
source_system: Call Report and FR Y-9C filings
what_it_shows: Average total consolidated assets of about $212 billion for the bank and about $226 billion for the holding company; the bank is about 94% of the parent

title: Group: intercompany agreement register
source_system: Group legal contract management system
what_it_shows: The 2021 intercompany services agreement, under which the Financial Software division runs the digital banking platform for the bank, sets no incident notice time and no audit rights. Group Property Management serves the bank under a 2019 property services agreement with security terms. CRE Lending services loans for the bank under an informal arrangement with no written servicing agreement. Outside vendor contract templates carry the group security schedule

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication, session and federation policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: 45,000 workforce identities. Number-matching MFA for all workforce; phishing-resistant hardware keys for administrators; lockout after 10 failed attempts with risk-based blocking; passwords of at least 14 characters screened against breached-password lists. Single sign-on sessions last 12 hours and are not bound to a device; no re-authentication is configured for sensitive console actions. The core and platform consoles and the CRE loan system (since 2025) federate to SYS-G1; the lease system uses local accounts. Sign-in pages show the group system use notice

title: Group: SYS-G1 identity governance and service account export
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1); platform team service account spreadsheet
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events for all divisions; quarterly certification campaigns; workforce accounts inactive 45 days disabled automatically; temporary and emergency accounts expire after 30 days; break-glass accounts sealed with an alert on use; identifiers unique and not reused for 2 years; account events sent to the SIEM; platform contractors carry a sponsor and an end date. 37 service accounts for the payment initiation gateway and platform pipelines are listed in a separate spreadsheet, were created outside identity governance, and are not in certification campaigns

title: Group: privileged access management inventory, policy and session logs
source_system: Privileged access management console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Administrators hold separate privileged accounts. Privileged access to core servers, platform clusters and databases is granted just in time with approval and session recording, and every privileged session and command is logged to the SIEM. Core software vendor maintenance uses named PAM accounts with MFA and recording; building controller vendor access also goes through PAM; engineer production access is time-bound

title: Group: Q1 2026 access certification results
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Quarterly certification of bank systems and of privileged and business roles completed by managers and data owners; service accounts are not in the campaigns

title: Group: endpoint configuration profile and zero-trust access policy
source_system: Endpoint management console; zero-trust access gateway
what_it_shows: Workstations lock after 10 minutes idle (branch and wire-room workstations after 5); laptops have full-disk encryption and remote wipe; teller workstations use application allow-listing; remote access only through zero-trust access with device posture checks and MFA, over TLS 1.2 or higher

title: Group: SIEM data sources, event logging list, use cases and correlation rules
source_system: Group SIEM (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC with real-time analysis and a case workflow. Identity, endpoint, network, data center, cloud, core and platform logs are onboarded and correlated, with an identity event dashboard and a SOC review log. The event logging list agreed for the core and platform covers sign-in, payment creation and approval, beneficiary and limit changes, entitlement changes, support console views and core maintenance; a sample audit record carries user, tenant, account, amount, beneficiary, device, source address, time and outcome. User behavior analytics flag atypical workforce sign-in and core activity. No use case or correlation rule covers sessions replayed from new infrastructure, support console activity, or inbox-rule creation in Commercial Real Estate mailboxes. Traffic is monitored at the hubs and data center edges

title: Group: SOC playbooks and incident case export, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: Group case management system (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: Incidents tracked in one case system with timelines and determination records under group playbooks, including BEC playbooks for bank wire operations and steps for account holds, evidence preservation and legal hold; a liaison named for each division. The playbooks do not say who decides to suspend platform functions for all tenants. Financial Software client incidents are scoped per client contract. Commercial Real Estate cases appear in the system from 2026; earlier division incidents were handled by the division IT manager

title: Group: EDR coverage report
source_system: EDR console (SYS-G2)
what_it_shows: EDR on every server, workstation and container node in both data centers and both cloud providers; container runtime protection on the platform

title: Group: vulnerability scan, patch and configuration compliance reports, Q1 2026
source_system: Vulnerability scanner; patch management console; guardrail policy service
what_it_shows: Weekly authenticated scans; aging report measured against 15 days for critical and 30 days for high findings; patch compliance report; data center servers scanned against hardened benchmarks; daily configuration compliance report for cloud resources against guardrail settings

title: Group: external penetration test report, 2026
source_system: Third-party testing firm report
what_it_shows: Annual independent external penetration test of the digital banking platform and the core interfaces; the engagement letter records a red-team exercise every 2 years

title: Group: email protection policy export
source_system: Email security gateway (SYS-G2); email and collaboration admin console (SYS-G4)
what_it_shows: Anti-phishing and spam filtering in the suite and in the gateway; external senders tagged; look-alike domains blocked; email encryption available; inbox-rule alerts not enabled for all mailboxes; no retention rule purges mailbox content

title: Group: information security program, policies and standards library
source_system: Group policy repository (intranet)
what_it_shows: One group information security program aligned to CSF 2.0: POL-01 to POL-05 (2025 versions), approved by the holding company board and adopted by the bank board. Group standards for logging and monitoring, change, configuration, resilience, cryptography (TLS 1.2 or higher; FIPS-validated modules), authorization, HR, third-party risk, supply chain risk management, platform engineering and records retention. Core and platform access procedures cover role requests, tenant administration and break-glass use

title: Group: division policy supplements and policy register
source_system: Group policy repository
what_it_shows: Banking supplement aligned to the 2025 group policies; Financial Software supplement v2025, last aligned 2025-11; Commercial Real Estate uses the acquired company's 2023 policy set, never aligned to group policy. The 2023 set says to confirm wire instruction changes by phone with the sender, provides general annual training only, routes incidents to the division IT manager, keeps closing email indefinitely, lists title and escrow agents on an approved list, and does not address control inheritance

title: Group: common control catalog, inheritance matrices and interconnection register
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: 100 group common controls for SYS-G1 to SYS-G4, each with a named provider. Inheritance is documented for the bank (2025 matrix) and in the Financial Software SOC 1 and SOC 2 system descriptions; no inheritance matrix exists for Commercial Real Estate. The interconnection register lists the core and platform connections to SYS-B2, the card processor, credit bureaus, client institutions' cores and the Federal Reserve payment services (through SYS-B2)

title: Group: board and board committee minutes and resolutions, 2025 to Q1 2026
source_system: Corporate secretary
what_it_shows: The holding company board approved the group program and the bank board adopted it as the bank's program in 2025-11. Annual information security reports went to both boards; the 2025 report to the bank board covers each III.F topic. Both board risk committees receive quarterly cyber reports. The bank board designated the Group CISO as the bank's information security officer. The bank board risk committee approved the risk governance framework in 2026-03. The bank board roster shows four independent directors, with annual director cyber and risk training recorded

title: Group: risk management strategy, 2025 registers, risk acceptances and monitoring reports
source_system: Group GRC tool
what_it_shows: Risk tolerance and acceptance authority by level (Low: division security and compliance lead; Moderate: division president; High: Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO; Very High: board risk committee); 2025 group, bank and Financial Software registers and no Commercial Real Estate register; risk acceptance records; a second-line challenge log; a monitoring strategy with monthly metrics to the executive risk committee; quarterly risk appetite reports and dashboard; the quarterly pack consolidates cyber risk data by hand from the registers

title: Group: internal audit charter, audit universe and 2026 audit plan
source_system: Group internal audit
what_it_shows: Internal audit reports to the holding company and bank audit committees and does not design or operate controls. The audit universe and root-cause reporting are defined. The 2026 plan schedules the common control assessment with division samples for July and August, including Commercial Real Estate for the first time. The 2025 assessment of the bank's risk governance framework by internal audit with an external party is on file. No earlier assessment of Commercial Real Estate controls is recorded

title: Group: disclosure committee charter and FY2025 Form 10-K Item 106 disclosure
source_system: SEC filings; corporate secretary
what_it_shows: The Item 106 disclosure describes board risk committee oversight and the Group CISO's reporting lines. The charter covers cybersecurity incidents and sets Form 8-K Item 1.05 review steps; divisions escalate incidents to the committee

title: Group: incident response plan v5, notification procedures and incident binder
source_system: Group SOC document library; Group legal
what_it_shows: Group incident response plan v5 (2025) with a Part 53 determination step and a determination log; Supplement A customer notice criteria, a notice template with each III.B item, a misuse determination worksheet and a mail and electronic notice procedure. The notification matrix covers the bank only. The plan does not mention the 2024 acquisition or the platform tenancy model. The offline incident binder lists the OCC supervisory office and the Federal Reserve point of contact, with backup contacts

title: Group: exercise reports and responder training records, 2025 to Q1 2026
source_system: Group SOC document library
what_it_shows: Technical playbooks, including the BEC playbooks for bank wire operations, exercised each quarter; no exercise combined the bank, the platform and Commercial Real Estate with the notification matrix. Incident responders trained each year

title: Group: training, social engineering exercise and acknowledgment records
source_system: Learning management system; phishing simulation platform
what_it_shows: 98.9% completion of annual security training; monthly reminders; quarterly social engineering exercises (email, voice and payment-change requests) in all divisions; POL-05 acknowledgments at hire and each year. The role training catalog assigns the payment-fraud module to bank wire, treasury and contact center staff and to platform support and payments staff; the module has no content on vendor-impersonation requests from clients. Commercial Real Estate closers and funding staff are assigned general annual training only

title: Group: HR standards, screening, termination, contractor and sanctions records
source_system: Group HR system
what_it_shows: Background checks before hire for all workforce, including the checks bank law requires for bank employees; HR termination events trigger access removal, with a 4-hour standard and immediate removal for involuntary terminations; platform contractors sign security terms and are listed with end dates; sanctions log; performance review templates for platform leaders include security objectives; succession plans exist for executives only

title: Group: accounts payable vendor master and third-party risk register
source_system: ERP vendor master; third-party risk management tool
what_it_shows: Tiered vendor program under a third-party risk policy and a supply chain risk management plan; critical vendors assessed each year. Vendors include cloud providers A and B, the identity, SIEM, EDR, email security and productivity SaaS vendors, the core software vendor, the card processor, the loan origination SaaS vendor, credit bureaus, the telephony vendor, the AML monitoring software vendor, the loan servicing and lease SaaS vendors, the building automation and alarm monitoring vendors, facility maintenance contractors, a certified destruction vendor, the source hosting, status page and support tool vendors, data aggregation partners, the enterprise AI and coding assistant vendors, carriers, a forensic retainer, the ERP and HR SaaS vendors, the payroll provider, a filing agent and the penetration testing firm. Vendor screening covers offshore and foreign-person access. The Financial Software division and CRE Lending are not in the register as service providers to the bank. Vendor exit plans have no test records

title: Group: vendor SOC reports on file and SOC review log
source_system: Vendor portals; third-party risk management tool
what_it_shows: Annual SOC report reviews and due diligence files for outside critical vendors: cloud providers A and B (SOC 2, covering physical access and media sanitization), the identity SaaS vendor (including lockout and sign-in features), the card processor (SOC 1), the core software vendor, the loan origination SaaS vendor and the loan servicing and lease SaaS vendors. Supply chain risk assessments for critical vendors. The log has no review of the Financial Software division's SOC reports. Bank-designated notice contacts were sent to the card processor, the core software vendor and the loan origination vendor

title: Group: AI use-case discovery
source_system: Model inventory; procurement records; SaaS discovery and SYS-G1 app list
what_it_shows: AI in use: the bank's AI credit underwriting model (consumer since 2025-10, small business since 2026-03), wire and ACH payment fraud scoring, AML alert prioritization, a contact center generative assistant used by 600 agents, the Financial Software cash-flow data service (64 client banks), platform fraud scoring for client tenants, an engineering coding assistant, a CRE underwriting assistant in pilot at 2 offices, building energy analytics, and an enterprise generative AI assistant piloted with 8,000 users. The generative tools and the coding assistant run under enterprise no-training terms

title: Group: records retention schedule, data inventory and privacy notices
source_system: Group records management; data inventory; privacy office
what_it_shows: Group records schedule: security logs kept 1 year searchable and 7 years archived; payment records on the bank schedule; client tenant data returned or destroyed at contract end; per-contract retention settings for platform data. The data inventory classifies client data as Restricted and lists Commercial Real Estate closing files, servicing records and tenant records. Group privacy notices cover non-GLBA personal information; there is no division-specific privacy review for Commercial Real Estate

title: Group: data center, cloud account and DR architecture inventory
source_system: CMDB; cloud provider consoles and cloud asset inventory (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Two group data centers, primary active and secondary hot, host SYS-B1 and SYS-B2 with synchronous replication of core and payments databases. Provider A hosts the landing zone hub, SYS-S1 (primary and warm standby regions), SYS-S2, credit model serving for SYS-B3 and the enterprise data platform; provider B hosts the immutable backup vault and the SYS-S1 disaster recovery copy of backups. Cloud roles federate from SYS-G1; the only local cloud users are sealed break-glass accounts. The payment initiation gateway runs as one cluster in the primary data center with a cold standby in the secondary. Branches have cellular failover. SYS-G1, SYS-G4, SYS-R1 and the lease system are SaaS. The component inventory for core, platform and gateway is generated from the CMDB and cloud inventory

title: Group: landing-zone guardrail, change and log archive policy report
source_system: Guardrail policy service; infrastructure code repository (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Guardrail policies enforce configuration settings and block unapproved services and ports in every division account; platform baselines are defined as code; only pipelines and PAM-elevated engineers can change production; the central log archive is immutable and readable only by the SOC

title: Group: network design and firewall policy export
source_system: Hub and data center firewall management; network documentation (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Hub and data center firewalls deny by default and segment division accounts; encrypted private links connect the data centers and provider A; payment requests reach the payments hub only from the platform payment API through the payment initiation gateway, over allow-listed private links with mutual TLS; building access control and automation controllers sit on separate segments at each site, with older controllers at some branches; SYS-B2 has dedicated connections to the Federal Reserve payment services

title: Group: key management inventory, encryption report and key age report
source_system: Provider key management services; data center HSM consoles (SYS-G3)
what_it_shows: Cloud key management with one group-managed key per platform tenant; hardware security modules in both data centers for core data and payment message signing; FIPS-validated module list; encryption at rest for core databases, platform databases and backups. 21 payment initiation gateway and pipeline service account keys are static and older than 1 year

title: Group: backup policy, vault configuration and restore test log
source_system: Backup service and immutable vault (provider B); data center backup console
what_it_shows: Daily immutable backups of core and platform databases to the provider B vault and the secondary data center, under a separate backup identity; restore tests recorded each quarter; nightly CRE loan system export to the group vault; building controller configurations backed up daily

title: Group: TLS configuration scan, Q1 2026

what_it_shows: External and inter-site endpoints accept TLS 1.2 or higher with approved cipher suites; private links to SYS-B2 use mutual TLS

title: Group: walk-through of the primary data center and an operations center
source_system: Primary data center and one operations center (observation)
what_it_shows: Badge plus biometric entry and mantraps in use; guards and video at entrances; access logs presented on request; the payment initiation gateway cluster is housed in the primary data center

title: Group: enterprise data platform extract configuration
source_system: Enterprise data platform (provider A)
owner: Group chief data and analytics officer
what_it_shows: Nightly extracts from the platform carry bank-tenant data only, and an extract filter blocks client tenant data; data sharing approved by the Group Chief Privacy Officer; access approvals recorded for analytics users

title: Banking: customer, channel and branch volumes
source_system: Core banking reporting (SYS-B1); digital banking reporting (SYS-S1)
what_it_shows: About 6.2 million consumer and 540,000 business customers; 4.1 million consumer and 310,000 business users on the digital banking platform; about 820 branches in Florida and 8 other southeastern and south-central states; 6 operations centers; two wire rooms and three contact centers in different states

title: Banking: payments hub and wire operations records
source_system: Payments hub (SYS-B2) configuration; wire operations procedures and daily volume report
what_it_shows: About 26,000 outgoing wires (about $34 billion) per business day through the Federal Reserve payment services and correspondents. Maker-checker on every outgoing wire. Callback to an independently verified number on file for new beneficiaries over $1 million; out-of-band confirmation from a second customer officer over $5 million. Payment approvals are stored with the approving user's authenticated session in the payment record. Payment messages are signed at the gateway and verified by SYS-B2. CRE Lending funding wires are released by bank wire operations as a business customer's wires

title: Banking: core banking (SYS-B1) role matrix, change records and support status
source_system: Core admin console; core role conflicts report; change records; support status report
what_it_shows: Core roles with conflicting combinations are blocked; core administrators cannot approve their own changes; file integrity monitoring on core servers; changes approved by the change advisory board with security review for high-risk changes; baseline configurations held as hardened images; the core operating system upgrade was completed in 2026-04, and the support status report lists no unsupported components

title: Banking: risk governance framework, risk appetite statement and reliance assessment
source_system: Bank independent risk management records
what_it_shows: Risk governance framework under 12 CFR 30 App. D, approved 2026-03, with cyber and technology risk inside operational risk in the taxonomy. Risk appetite statement with two cyber limits: no High cyber risk untreated for more than two quarters, and payment-instruction fraud losses under $25 million a year. A breach protocol written for financial limits. Quarterly risk limit reports from bank technology and operations units. A documented assessment of the bank's reliance on group components (cyber, third-party, model risk), shared with the OCC in 2026-03

title: Banking: contingency plans, criticality analysis and recovery runbooks
source_system: Bank continuity library
what_it_shows: Core contingency plan for data center failover, with failover tests twice a year; payments contingency plan and digital channels plan, whose scenarios are data center and region failover; a criticality analysis naming the payment initiation gateway, the core database cluster, the customer identity service and key management; recovery runbooks that restore core, gateway and platform in order and validate balances and payment queues. No gateway failover test is recorded

title: Banking: outside vendor contracts and SOC review files
source_system: Bank vendor management
what_it_shows: Card processor (debit authorization, ATM driving and card fraud monitoring, with stand-in limits; SOC 1), core software vendor and loan origination SaaS vendor contracts carry the group security schedule and prompt incident notice terms, with a SOC review file for each. The card processor holds card data; the platform shows masked card numbers only. ATMs use anti-skimming devices and hardened images

title: Banking: AI credit model (AI-001) documentation and validation file
source_system: Model inventory; model risk management validation reports; model release records; scoring log
what_it_shows: In-house gradient-boosted model served on provider A (SYS-B3); version pinned and hashed and released only after model risk management approval; every score logged with version, inputs, reason codes and decision. Consumer installment loans up to $50,000 since 2025-10 (validated 2025-09), about 70% decided automatically inside credit policy cutoffs; small business lines up to $250,000 since 2026-03 (validated 2026-02), decided by underwriters. Cash-flow attributes from the Financial Software data service were added in 2026-03 and re-validated for performance. The reason code mapping is dated before the 2026-03 attribute change. Pre-deployment fairness testing is recorded for consumer loans. The model does not use age

title: Banking: bank tenant settings on the digital banking platform
source_system: Bank tenant console and customer identity service settings (SYS-S1)
what_it_shows: Business payment users must use MFA; consumers use risk-based MFA, and SMS one-time codes are still accepted; device binding; step-up for new beneficiaries and payments above limits; a second approver for business wires over $10,000; a daily report of beneficiary and limit changes reviewed by the bank; entitlement changes approved by two treasury management officers; payment files reconciled daily; staff limit and entitlement changes in the console have no re-authentication step

title: Banking: BSA/AML records and SAR log
source_system: BSA/AML case management; transaction monitoring system
what_it_shows: SARs filed by the bank BSA/AML Officer under 12 CFR 21.11, with security incidents linked to SAR cases; AML alert prioritization with sampling below the threshold; a nonbank BSA/AML Officer is named; the case log shows Commercial Real Estate fraud cases handled informally by the bank's BSA team

title: Banking: threat intelligence reports and quarterly program review minutes

what_it_shows: Threat intelligence reports delivered to the bank; quarterly program reviews track changes after the 2024 acquisition; a bank regulatory change management process

title: Financial Software: client and contract register
source_system: Financial Software contract management system
what_it_shows: 310 client institutions: 212 banks (74 OCC-supervised, 31 state member banks, 107 FDIC-supervised state nonmember banks) and 98 credit unions, in 38 states; about 19 million end users across all tenants, including the bank's; about 2,300 client administrators; no federal agency customers. A security schedule in every master agreement. Incident notice terms sit in individual contracts: 72 hours standard, 24 hours in 88 contracts, 5 business days for credit unions. 64 client banks buy the cash-flow data service, 3 of them in Colorado. The implementation checklist includes a service relationship notice letter for each new client. A commitments register lists client service commitments

title: Financial Software: client notice procedure, contact register and maintenance calendar
source_system: Client risk and assurance records; CRM
what_it_shows: Bank-designated notice contacts (12 CFR 53.4(a)(1)) on file for 151 of 212 client banks; CEO and CIO contacts for the others kept by account managers in the CRM; no designated contact on file for the bank tenant. The notice procedure is not tied to a timer in the incident tool, and the notice register does not hold contract notice times. Maintenance calendar published 30 days ahead; status page for outage notices

title: Financial Software: SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 reports, period ending 2025-09-30
source_system: Financial Software client risk and assurance office
what_it_shows: Both reports issued 2025-12-12 for the 12 months ending 2025-09-30, with unmodified opinions. The SOC 2 report covers Security, Availability and Confidentiality for the digital banking platform, with group identity, SOC and infrastructure services included and cloud provider A carved out. One SOC 2 exception: CC6.2, 2 of 40 sampled support leavers removed after the 4-hour target (within 2 days). The descriptions list complementary user entity controls (5 in SOC 1; the same 5 plus a designated notice contact in SOC 2) and do not describe the cash-flow data service. Neither report states incident notice terms. A log of bridge letters issued on request

title: Financial Software: platform (SYS-S1) architecture and tenant security settings report
source_system: Platform architecture repository; tenant administration console (SYS-S1)
what_it_shows: Container platform, API gateway and managed databases in provider A, in a primary region with a warm standby region and continuous replication; one schema and key per tenant; a dedicated database cluster for the bank tenant; the support console is separated from payment functions; tenant isolation and authorization tests run each release; the API validates beneficiary, amount, routing and limit fields; security functions are limited to named security and platform engineering roles. Each tenant can switch off MFA for business payment users; 41 of 310 client tenants have done so. The customer identity service applies device binding and risk scoring. Capacity monitoring with headroom targets; WAF, DDoS protection and rate limits

title: Financial Software: support console role export
source_system: Support console (SYS-S1)

title: Commercial Real Estate: loan system (SYS-R1) configuration, user list and audit export
